verdict.line: You win by forcing all-ins before level 6 while Gwen's Hallowed Mist and Skip 'n Slash cooldowns are still long; you lose if the lane stalls past 20 minutes and her passive true damage and split-push safety take over.

brief.thesis: Gwen has no reliable way to punish a committed dash-stun combo before she has points in W (Hallowed Mist), so Irelia's early kill pressure is real — but the head-to-head win rate sits at 46.4% over 343 games because Gwen's Skip 'n Slash cooldown refund and A Thousand Cuts passive let her out-scale and out-safety Irelia once teamfights and split-push windows open up. This is a lane you have to close out, not coast through.

theirWindow.when: Mist is up and she's near cover
theirWindow.what: She can cast W (Hallowed Mist, cooldown 22/21/20/19/18s) and become untargetable to anyone outside it, then poke free with Q (Snip Snip!) or bait your engage. Don't commit Q (Bladesurge) into her while Mist is available — you'll dash in and eat true damage with no way to finish the trade.

yourWindow.when: Both Mist and Skip 'n Slash are down
yourWindow.what: Open with E (Flawless Duet, cooldown 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s) to stun and Mark her, then Q (Bladesurge) refreshes off the Mark for a second dash and heal — that's your full burst-and-sustain combo and it's unavailable to her while E (Skip 'n Slash, cooldown 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s) is on cooldown.

start.why: Run in 87.1% of games at a 45.8% win rate — the sustain and early AD let you contest trades into Snip Snip! poke without burning summoners.

boots.why: Picked in 61.8% of games at 43.9% win rate — Gwen's Q, R, and passive all deal magic/true damage, so the flat MR matters more here than the armor from Plated Steelcaps.

core.why: First item in the highest-win-rate path (56.8% over 37 games) — the current-health damage and slow let you punish her low base health before she stacks defenses.
Second in that 56.8% path — magic resist directly answers her Q/passive/R magic damage and adds attack speed for extra Ionian Fervor stacks.
Closes out the 56.8% core — once you're ahead, Hullbreaker punishes her split-push plan by letting you outduel her at towers.

runes.keystoneWhy: The 53.7% win-rate page runs Conqueror — you need the sustained healing to survive extended trades into a champion whose passive heals her back on every hit.

summoners.why: Run in 86.4% of games at 47.2% win rate — with solo-kill advantage on your side, Ignite converts your level 3-5 all-in window into an actual kill instead of a reset.

playing.title: All-in before level 6
playing.detail: Land E (Flawless Duet) for the stun and Mark, then Q (Bladesurge) to dash, heal, and refresh off the Mark. This is your highest-damage window before her Hallowed Mist cooldown is short enough to bail her out.

playing.title: Don't trust W against her burst
playing.detail: W (Defiant Dance) only reduces physical damage while charging — Gwen's Snip Snip! center bolt is true damage and her passive/R hits are magic, so W won't save you from her actual damage source.

playing.title: Track Skip 'n Slash, not just Mist
playing.detail: If she just used E (Skip 'n Slash) and didn't hit you, its cooldown (13/12.5/12/11.5/11s) is full length — that's your window to walk up and threaten Q (Bladesurge) without her dashing away.

playing.title: Play for max Ionian Fervor stacks before committing
playing.detail: Your passive's bonus attack speed and on-hit damage cap out with repeated spell hits — chain Q into auto into E so you're at full stacks when the stun lands, not before.

playing.title: Wall her escape with R
playing.detail: R (Vanguard's Edge) fires blades that Mark and damage on hit, then leaves a wall that slows and damages anyone who walks through it — drop it behind her dash path so Skip 'n Slash can't cleanly disengage.

playing.title: Don't stand still in Snip Snip!
playing.detail: The center of her Q deals true damage and applies her passive — sidestep after the first snip lands rather than trading autos through all six casts.

playing.title: Close the game, don't scale past it
playing.detail: The 46.4% head-to-head win rate comes from late-game split-push, not lane — take plates and force objectives once you're ahead instead of playing a long scaling lane.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win-rate/pick-rate numbers above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and trade-pattern advice are my own analysis of the ability kits, not measured data.
